region: Mountain glaciers of NE Siberia and Kamchatka (GLACIMONTIS "East Siberian Mountains")
about: The MAXIMUM extent recorded at each glacier’s own local glacial maximum, anywhere between 57,000 and 14,000 years ago — not a single moment, and not comparable with the time slices the other three ice sources are drawn in. Different glaciers here peaked at different times.
source: Lima, A.C., Dulfer, H.E., Hughes, A.L.C., Margold, M., Barr, I., Laabs, B.J.C. & Flantua, S.G.A. (2026). Mountain glacier extents at the Last Glacial Maximum. Scientific Data 13, 629. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-026-06841-z
changes: Changes were made: the Filtered Reconstructed Paleoglaciers layer was restricted to the records the database itself classifies as East Siberian Mountains, reprojected from Web Mercator to WGS84, simplified at 1 km and rounded to 0.001 degrees; nothing else.
